result.title: A Valid Watermark Is Not a Valid Identity: Spatial-Spectral Adversarial Face Evasion with Watermark Preservation
result.comment: Accepted at IEEE International Joint Conference on Biometrics (IJCB 2026)
result.summary: Facial image watermarking can support traceability and certification in biometric pipelines, but provenance or manipulation detection alone does not guarantee reliable biometric identity. We introduce a watermark-preserving face evasion attack that targets this gap under a black-box watermarking setting, without access to the watermarking components. The proposed PGD-L_2 attack guides adversarial perturbations with spatial and spectral preservation terms to reduce face-recognition similarity while limiting pixel-level distortion and high-frequency changes that may interfere with hidden watermark cues. Evaluated on controlled facial images with two watermarking schemes, two face-recognition models, and two datasets, the attack achieves evasion rates above 92% at operational thresholds while preserving watermark recovery above 93% for StegaFormer and above 99.7% for FaceSigns, with visual quality above 47dB PSNR at epsilon_2=2.0. These results expose a structural gap in watermark-based facial certification: a face image can remain watermark-valid and visually faithful while becoming biometrically unreliable.

AI.brief_summary: 提出一种在保留人脸水印的前提下实施的黑盒人脸规避攻击（PGD-L_2），通过空间与频谱保持项让扰动降低人脸识别相似度，同时维持水印可恢复性与视觉质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究的是生物特征认证中水印有效性与身份可靠性的脱节，涉及对抗扰动与频谱保持，但与 VLM 内部推理状态、视觉证据使用或 latent 生成方式没有可核查的具体联系。
